date-drill.sql:
-- 'quarter' comes from the grain switch
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.ordered_at) AS period,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.ordered_at)
ORDER BY DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.ordered_at);

-- the reader clicked Q2 2026: new range, finer grain
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at) AS period,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.ordered_at >= DATE '2026-04-01'
  AND o.ordered_at < DATE '2026-07-01'
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at)
ORDER BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at);

fiscal-calendar.sql:
-- July starts the fiscal year, pasted into every report
SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM o.ordered_at)
    + CASE WHEN EXTRACT(month FROM o.ordered_at) > 6
      THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS fiscal_year,
  CASE WHEN EXTRACT(month FROM o.ordered_at) > 9 THEN 2
    WHEN EXTRACT(month FROM o.ordered_at) > 6 THEN 1
    WHEN EXTRACT(month FROM o.ordered_at) > 3 THEN 4
    ELSE 3 END AS fiscal_quarter,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

as-of-anchor.sql:
-- "last 30 days" counts back from the newest order
SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.ordered_at > (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders)
    - INTERVAL '30 days';

-- and again in every other query on the page
SELECT c.country, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.ordered_at > (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders)
    - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY c.country;

partial-period.sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at) AS month,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue,
  MAX(o.ordered_at) AS last_order_day
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
-- the app checks last_order_day against the month's end

period-compare.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at) AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY 1
), filled AS (
  -- months with no orders still need a row
  SELECT s.m AS month, COALESCE(r.revenue, 0) AS revenue
  FROM generate_series(DATE '2025-06-01',
    DATE '2026-09-01', INTERVAL '1 month') s(m)
  LEFT JOIN monthly r ON r.month = s.m
)
SELECT month, revenue,
  revenue / NULLIF(LAG(revenue, 1) OVER w, 0) - 1
    AS vs_prev_month,
  revenue / NULLIF(LAG(revenue, 12) OVER w, 0) - 1
    AS vs_last_year
FROM filled
WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY month)
ORDER BY month;

custom-compare.sql:
-- both ranges come from the reader's date pickers
SELECT c.country,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.ordered_at BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01'
      AND DATE '2025-12-31'
    THEN oi.quantity * p.price END) AS h2_2025,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.ordered_at BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND DATE '2026-06-30'
    THEN oi.quantity * p.price END) AS h1_2026
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.ordered_at BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01'
  AND DATE '2026-06-30'
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY h1_2026 DESC;

to-date.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at) AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY 1
), filled AS (
  -- months with no orders still need a row
  SELECT s.m AS month, COALESCE(r.revenue, 0) AS revenue
  FROM generate_series(DATE '2025-06-01',
    DATE '2026-09-01', INTERVAL '1 month') s(m)
  LEFT JOIN monthly r ON r.month = s.m
)
SELECT month, revenue,
  SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY EXTRACT(year FROM month)
    ORDER BY month) AS ytd,
  SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month
    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS trailing_3m
FROM filled
ORDER BY month;

hierarchy-drill.sql:
-- level 3: customers in APAC › Australia
SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN countries m ON m.name = c.country
WHERE m.region = 'APAC' AND c.country = 'Australia'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

-- level 4: Customer 184's orders, the path comes along
SELECT o.id, o.ordered_at, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN countries m ON m.name = c.country
WHERE m.region = 'APAC' AND c.country = 'Australia'
  AND c.id = 184
GROUP BY o.id, o.ordered_at
ORDER BY o.ordered_at DESC;

adhoc-breakdown.sql:
-- o.status comes from the "Break down by" menu,
-- 'Software' from the clicked bar
SELECT o.status AS breakdown,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE p.category = 'Software'
GROUP BY o.status
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

underlying-records.sql:
-- the clicked cell is Japan × Software, page 2
SELECT o.id, o.ordered_at, c.name, o.status,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.country = 'Japan' AND p.category = 'Software'
GROUP BY o.id, o.ordered_at, c.name, o.status
ORDER BY o.ordered_at DESC, o.id DESC
LIMIT 25 OFFSET 25;

drillthrough.sql:
-- opened as /apps/reports/cohort-heatmap?country=Japan,
-- the app parses country= and pastes it back in
WITH firsts AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(o.ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
  WHERE c.country = 'Japan'
  GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATE_DIFF('month', f.cohort, o.ordered_at) AS month_n,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customers
FROM firsts f
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = f.customer_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

metric-switch.sql:
-- 'units' comes from the switch, and each switch reruns it
SELECT p.category,
  CASE 'units'
    WHEN 'revenue' THEN SUM(oi.quantity * p.price)
    WHEN 'orders' THEN COUNT(DISTINCT o.id)
    WHEN 'units' THEN SUM(oi.quantity)
  END AS value
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY value DESC;

dimension-switch.sql:
-- o.status comes from the dropdown, mapped from an
-- allow-list: country → c.country, category → p.category
SELECT o.status AS grp,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY o.status
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

sort.sql:
-- 'orders DESC' comes from the clicked header;
-- page 2 must repeat it, with a tiebreaker
SELECT c.name, c.country,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS orders
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.country
ORDER BY orders DESC, c.id
LIMIT 25 OFFSET 25;

top-n.sql:
WITH by_country AS (
  SELECT c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.country
), ranked AS (
  SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
  FROM by_country
)
-- 3 comes from the Top N menu
SELECT CASE WHEN rnk <= 3 THEN country ELSE 'Other' END
    AS country,
  SUM(revenue) AS revenue
FROM ranked
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY MAX(rnk);

pivot.sql:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT c.country, p.category, oi.quantity * p.price AS rev
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
)
-- one column per category, typed by hand
SELECT country,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Services' THEN rev END) AS serv,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Software' THEN rev END) AS soft,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Hardware' THEN rev END) AS hard,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Parts' THEN rev END) AS parts,
  SUM(rev) AS total
FROM r
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY total DESC;

totals.sql:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT p.category, p.name,
    SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY p.category, p.name
)
-- the app still draws the subtotal rows itself
SELECT category, name, revenue,
  SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS cat_total,
  revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY category)
    AS share,
  SUM(revenue) OVER () AS grand_total
FROM r
ORDER BY category, revenue DESC;

percent-of-total.sql:
SELECT c.country,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price)
    / NULLIF(SUM(SUM(oi.quantity * p.price)) OVER (), 0)
    AS share
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
-- the reader's category filter
WHERE p.category = 'Software'
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

cumulative-moving.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.ordered_at) AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY 1
), filled AS (
  -- months with no orders still need a row
  SELECT s.m AS month, COALESCE(r.revenue, 0) AS revenue
  FROM generate_series(DATE '2025-06-01',
    DATE '2026-09-01', INTERVAL '1 month') s(m)
  LEFT JOIN monthly r ON r.month = s.m
)
SELECT month, revenue,
  SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS running_total,
  AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month
    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_3m
FROM filled
ORDER BY month;

drill-path.sql:
-- step 4, ↑ APAC: the app drops the country condition
SELECT c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN countries m ON m.name = c.country
WHERE m.region = 'APAC'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC;

-- step 5, ↓ Singapore: and adds it back with the new value
SELECT c.name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN countries m ON m.name = c.country
WHERE m.region = 'APAC' AND c.country = 'Singapore'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

row-actions.sql:
SELECT c.name,
  'https://crm.example.com/accounts/'
    || CAST(c.id AS VARCHAR) AS crm_url,
  'mailto:' || c.email
    || '?subject=Your%20order%20history' AS email_url,
  SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 8;
